but_it_is_loud: A flip is not silent. Measured on this bench rows: with one CLEAN rate flipped, RC 36 reports n=3 where the clean offset gives n=4 - a wrong integer - but the residual goes from 0.026 to 0.360 against a published worst of 0.04, and RC 28 comes out at n=-1, which is impossible. Two independent tells, both in the printed table.
change_made: tools/issue48_lattice.py now refuses the integers when any n comes out negative, and names the CLEAN set as the usual cause. Additive; the offset rule itself is unchanged and is linux-x1 to rule on.
means: Two of the three rates the offset is drawn from are bimodal with a second mode exactly 2/256 down, on two benches each. Only RC 56 is single-moded. The offset every published lattice integer is measured against is a mean over a contaminated set.
not_claimed: That any published integer is wrong. On the pooled rows the three rules agree to 0.024 of a step, so no reported n moves today. The defect is conditional on a batch drawing enough low reps, and it has not been observed doing so.
proposed: Drop 28 and 52 from CLEAN, or take each rate high mode instead of its median.
